en: The Eight Verses on Candraśekhara
O Moon-crested One, O Moon-crested One, O Moon-crested One, protect me!
O Moon-crested One, O Moon-crested One, O Moon-crested One, guard me!
[He who has] the jewel-peaked mountain as His bow and the silver mountain peak as His abode.

I take refuge in the moon-crested Lord, who has made the lord of serpents his bowstring, whose arrow is the face of Acyuta, who swiftly burnt the three cities, and who is worshipped by the inhabitants of heaven; what indeed can my salutation do for him? 2.
I bow to Bhava, the imperishable destroyer of worldly existence, whose two lotus feet are adorned with the fragrance of the flowers of the five trees,
whose body was once consumed by the fire born from the eye on his forehead,
and whose form is now anointed with ashes.
O Moon-crested One... [3] ...He who is enchanting with an upper garment made from the hide of a preeminent intoxicated elephant,
and whose lotus-feet are worshipped by the lotus-eyed one seated upon a lotus throne.
Wearing matted locks white and sprinkled by the spray from the waves of the celestial river,
the moon-crested one... [4] the friend of the king of Yakṣas, the remover of Bhaga’s eyes, adorned with serpents.
...whose beautiful left body is adorned by the daughter of the King of Mountains,
whose neck is dark blue from drinking poison, who wields an axe, who holds a deer, and who has the moon as his crest-ornament... 5
The Lord of the World, whose earrings are coiled like the lordly serpent Kuṇḍalīśvara, who has the bull as his vehicle, whose majesty is praised by the lords of sages such as Nārada,
the celestial wish-fulfilling tree for those who have taken refuge in him despite being blind with sin, and the ender of Death himself; [I bow to him].
O Moon-crested One...
[I bow] to the medicine for those diseased by worldly existence, the remover of all calamities,
the destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice, whose nature consists of the three qualities, and who possesses three eyes.
O Candraśekhara, [I bow to You] who bestows the fruit of devotion and liberation, who destroys all attachments,
who is compassionate toward Your devotees, who is worshipped, who is an inexhaustible treasure, and who is clothed in yellow garments.
To the Lord of all beings, the highest of the high, immeasurable, and unsurpassed;
whose form consists of the moon, water, sky, fire, soma-juice, wind, and ether;
O Moon-crested One... 8
To Him who performs the creation of the universe, who is again intent upon its protection,
and who likewise withdraws the entire phenomenal world with all its inhabitants;
who sports day and night accompanied by the hosts of the Lord of Ganas.
O Moon-crested One...
Whoever, in the presence of Śiva, recites this hymn composed by the son of Mṛkaṇḍu when he was terrified of death— wherever that person may be— fear of death shall indeed never befall them.
Candraśekhara alone bestows upon him a full lifespan, freedom from disease, the attainment of all goals, and devotion; he grants liberation effortlessly.
Thus ends the Śrī Candraśekharāṣṭaka Stotra.
